<!-- generated from maestro item 1290 — do not edit; the board item is the source of truth -->
Operators need one Communications workspace to configure SES domains and mailboxes, verify and repair their AWS setup, investigate delivery failures, maintain reusable templates, and work public contact requests. The safe version preserves the proven web-mojo workflows while replacing provider secrets in onboarding with managed DNS, keeping AWS credentials write-only, and making every external action explicit. SES account quota remains unavailable until the backend exposes it, but that does not block domain operations or message investigation.

---

## Spec

Agent-facing from here down. **Kind**: feature · **Requested by**: Ian Starnes · **Parent**: #1260 “Admin program — port ALL admin domains, use-case driven (epic)” · **Depends on**: #1305 FormWizard/Tabs; #1430 DNS domains/records for the managed-DNS adapter/link seam used by this wave build

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add dual-mount Communications Admin sections for SES email and Contact Messages. Email routes require global `sys.manage_aws` or `sys.comms`; contact-message routes and controls use the exact global support authorities below. Active-group membership must never open either Admin surface.
- [ ] Add typed definitions for `/api/aws/email/domain`, `/mailbox`, `/sent`, `/template`, `/send`, domain `onboard`/`audit`/`reconcile`, and `/api/account/public_message`, with safe graphs, parameter allowlists, exact envelopes, and response sanitation at the client boundary.
- [ ] Provide Email Domains, Mailboxes, Sent Messages, Email Templates, and Contact Messages tables. Preserve server search/filter/sort/paging, URL state, safe explicit exports, and KISS record-detail modals; add no `:id` routes, RightPanel, raw JSON inspector, or generic secret-bearing DataView.
- [ ] Domain administration must support create/edit, write-only AWS credential replacement, guided onboarding, audit, reconcile, and deletion with exact side-effect warnings. Create requires armed consent because the backend runs best-effort SES audit/reconcile; success says only that the row was created and always refetches. Delete states that local audit rows are erased while AWS/DNS resources may remain orphaned. The domain table never fakes `can_send`/`can_recv`.
- [ ] Build onboarding with #1305 FormWizard. Prefer the backend’s `use_dnsman: true` path, which selects the provider and stored DNS credential server-side; never port the deprecated GoDaddy key/secret request fields. Manual mode must show the complete returned verification/DKIM/MAIL-FROM records. When #1430 is present and the operator can view DNS, link to its domain/record surface by normalized domain name instead of building a second record editor.
- [ ] Audit uses imperative POST, no automatic retry, explicit confirmation, safe structured output, and `finally` refetch because it persists readiness fields. Reconcile/onboarding are likewise explicit, single-flight external actions.
- [ ] Mailboxes support CRUD and a deliberate test-send/template-send flow using only fields the handler actually forwards. Sending is imperative/uncached/single-flight and requires a sender/recipient confirmation. A 2xx `SentMessage(status='failed')` is a failed delivery attempt; successful submission remains `sending` until webhook updates.
- [ ] Sent Messages remain an immutable, day-grouped delivery log. Strip context/arbitrary metadata before Query/export. HTML preview uses a bare sandbox, `referrerPolicy="no-referrer"`, an offline CSP (`default-src 'none'; img-src data:; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; font-src 'none'; connect-src 'none'; frame-src 'none'; media-src 'none'; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'`), and neutralized anchors/meta refresh so opening a modal makes zero external requests.
- [ ] Email Templates support CRUD, subject/HTML/text editing with #1305 Tabs, and sandboxed HTML preview. Exports contain identifiers and timestamps only, never template bodies or metadata.
- [ ] Contact Messages use `sys.view_support`/`sys.security`/`sys.support` for reading, `sys.manage_support`/`sys.security`/`sys.support` for open/closed updates, and only `sys.manage_support` for deletion. Add the missing `view_support` and `manage_support` permission labels without changing category-rollup semantics. A manage-only grant does not imply view; grant both for a granular operator.
- [ ] Contact Messages support kind/status filters, server search, individual and batch open/closed changes, a PII-aware KISS detail modal, and a `mailto:` handoff only after validating one mailbox recipient. Render allowlisted metadata only and state that additional metadata was withheld. Safe export omits message body, IP, user agent, and metadata.
- [ ] Raw AWS keys/secrets, provider credentials, `mojo_secrets`, template contexts, and provider-shaped audit/error values must never enter caches, exports, logs, diagnostics, URLs, clipboard, or rendered error interpolation. Use per-resource allowlisted projections plus bounded text redaction; drop unknown nested audit/metadata fields. Secret-bearing writes bypass MutationCache.
- [ ] Extend the mock with exact graphs, paging, permissions, state transitions, manual/DNSMan onboarding, audit persistence, reconcile results, sending, CRUD/cascades, and public-message scoping. The mock must discard submitted credential plaintext after deriving masks and must reuse #1430’s DNS record store when managed onboarding applies records.
- [ ] Add package documentation, an executable showcase demo, targeted verification, and light/dark browser evidence in both the Portal shell and showcase. Automated and routine live verification is read-only; no domain create, audit, onboarding, reconcile, credential change, send, or delete runs against a live backend without explicit authorization for that exact action.

### Investigation

- **What exists**: web-mojo ships `src/extensions/admin/models/Email.js`, the five email/contact table pages, and four detail views. Portal-mojo already supplies AdminSection dual mounting, global scope clearing, ModelTable, DetailView/modal, SchemaForm, confirmations, safe exporters, Query sanitation hooks, and exact mock infrastructure; no messaging Admin module exists at commit `94b5aac`.
- **Live authority**: django-mojo source mounts the current endpoints under `/api/aws/email/*`; `docs/web_developer/email/email.md` still documents obsolete `/api/aws/emailtemplate`, `/api/aws/mailbox`, and `/api/aws/sentmessage` paths and is not the implementation contract.
- **Email permissions**: every current AWS email RestMeta/custom endpoint accepts global `manage_aws` or `comms` for both reads and writes. The UI gate is therefore `['sys.manage_aws', 'sys.comms']`; there is no distinct read-only email operator today.
- **Support permissions**: `PublicMessage.RestMeta` declares view `view_support|security|support`, save `manage_support|security|support`, and delete only `manage_support`, with `GROUP_FIELD='group'`. Global Admin must pin these to `sys.*`; group-scoped operators remain outside this surface.
- **Graph corrections**: `EmailDomain`’s default graph returns masked AWS values but omits `can_send` and `can_recv`; readiness is available in the audit response, not list rows. `SentMessage.basic` is the safe list graph; default includes bodies, BCC, `template_context`, status reason, and metadata. `PublicMessage.list` omits body/metadata/IP/user-agent while default detail includes them.
- **External side effects**: `EmailDomain.on_rest_created()` performs best-effort audit/reconcile and swallows failures; audit GET persists status/readiness; reconcile mutates SES/SNS/receiving configuration; onboarding mutates SES and optionally DNS; `/email/send` sends real mail. These are not routine live-test calls.
- **DNS integration**: `/domain/<id>/onboard` accepts `use_dnsman:true`; django-mojo matches the DNSMan domain by normalized name and applies records using its linked credential. Raw `godaddy_key`/`godaddy_secret` are deprecated. #1430 owns the record editor, so this item displays returned records and links there but never edits provider records itself.
- **Quota gap**: #1310 is still inbox and no quota endpoint exists. It degrades rather than blocks: omit the quota card/requests and document the gap; do not invent a mock-only endpoint or guess a future shape.
- **Dependencies**: #1305 is a build-order dependency for the onboarding wizard and template tabs. #1430 is reusable when installed but cannot be a deployment prerequisite because AWS email works without dnsman; manual record output remains complete.
- **Constraints**: HTML bodies/templates are untrusted operator or message content; the main document must never render them through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Domain/mailbox deletes cascade into operational/audit rows and need explicit consequences.
- **Out of scope**: incoming-email inbox/attachment UI, SES send quota, requesting SES production access, a second DNS editor, backend/model/migration changes, public contact submission forms, reply delivery, live production mutation during verification, and changing the shared client/envelope core.

## Plan

### Objective

Ship a reusable, exact, secret-safe Communications administrator that covers SES setup and delivery investigation plus the public contact queue, using the live django-mojo contract, FormWizard/Tabs, DNSMan composition, KISS modals, and an executable mock.

### Implementation

1. Add `packages/portal-mojo/src/admin/messaging/sanitize.ts`.
   - Implement explicit per-resource allowlisted projections for domain, audit, onboard/reconcile, send, sent-message, template, and public-message data. Unknown nested provider/audit/metadata fields are dropped, not humanized.
   - Add a bounded text redactor for thrown/backend error strings before any render/log/diagnostic seam. It removes credential/authorization/token material and truncates provider output without trying to preserve raw nested error payloads.
   - Preserve only `aws_key_masked`/`aws_secret_masked` on domains; remove raw and nested secret-shaped values before a helper returns to UI or Query.
   - Add separate safe row/detail/export projections: domain exports exclude masks, metadata, bucket/topic values; sent exports exclude bodies, BCC, context, metadata, and raw status payloads; template exports exclude bodies/metadata; public-message exports exclude body, IP, user agent, and metadata.

Domain search is name/region/status; mailbox search is email; sent search is subject/SES message id; template search is name; public-message search is name/email/subject/message. Allow only supported sort/filter keys and discard crafted graph/download/filename inputs before they become query keys or requests.

Create is preceded by armed consent naming SES/SNS/receipt-rule effects, reports only “row created; AWS convergence is best effort,” and always refetches because create-time audit/reconcile failures are swallowed.

Exact onboard fields are `use_dnsman`, region, receiving/S3 settings, MAIL FROM settings, and nested endpoints; never accept/send deprecated provider credentials or per-call AWS credentials.

Treat returned `status:'failed'` as a failed attempt even under HTTP 2xx, and `sending` as accepted/pending rather than delivered.

### Design Decisions

- #1305 is a hard build-order dependency; do not build a local wizard/tab fallback. #1430 lands first in this wave to provide the optional runtime DNS adapter and canonical numeric-id link seam; deployments may still omit DNSMan and use complete manual instructions.
- #1310 does not block this item. Delivery debugging comes from SentMessage status/reason and domain audit; quota remains absent rather than fabricated.
- The current backend has one email permission tier, so the UI does not invent a view-only email role. Contact Messages retain their separate support permission model.
- Manual DNS remains a complete result surface. Managed DNS failure never silently retries manually because SES-side work may already have happened.
- Sent/template HTML is isolated in a sandboxed iframe. The application document never trusts it.
- Secret-bearing writes and action results remain imperative/local; only sanitized model rows enter Query cache.

### Verification

- **Tier:** targeted
- **Run:** `npm run verify:admin-messaging`; `npm run verify:admin-navigation`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build`; `npm run build -w showcase`; `git diff --check`
- **Why:** Runtime behavior is bounded to one new messaging Admin module, additive `/api/aws/email/*` and `/api/account/public_message` mock branches, two additive Admin registry entries, and two permission-catalog labels. The dedicated verifier covers the wire, authorization, side-effect, sandbox, and secret boundaries; the existing navigation verifier covers shared route/menu composition; typecheck and both builds cover exported React composition. There are no migrations, backend changes, or shared client-core changes requiring a full tier.

### Challenge

- **Amended — SES side effects:** create requires armed consent, reports best-effort convergence, and refetches; delete explicitly distinguishes erased local audit history from orphaned AWS/DNS resources.
- **Amended — audit/send truth:** audit uses imperative POST/no retry/`finally` refetch; send types only executable fields and treats 2xx failed rows as failed attempts while `sending` remains pending.
- **Amended — safety projections:** per-resource allowlists plus bounded text redaction replace deny-key-only sanitation; unknown metadata/audit/provider payloads are withheld.
- **Amended — offline HTML:** exact CSP, bare sandbox, no-referrer, neutralized links/meta refresh, and zero-network browser evidence are required.
- **Amended — DNS/FormWizard dependencies:** #1305 must land with its challenged contract; #1430 provides an optional adapter/name-to-id URL seam and shared mock registration before messaging builds.
- **Amended — mailbox/contact fidelity:** the UI blocks mismatches that live generic save may accept; mock preserves direct-request parity; `mailto:` requires one validated mailbox.
- **Amended — verification/order:** messaging leaf modules land after #1305/#1430; root integrates shared registries and reruns every affected verifier, navigation, typecheck, both builds, and `git diff --check`.
- **Rebutted — permission matrix:** exact email/support view/manage/delete gates remain as scoped, including manage-without-view and no `comms` expansion.
- **Rebutted — KISS modals:** one list route per resource with native detail/result modals remains the correct Admin convention.
